Hurricane Irma was an extremely powerful and devastating ___E:tropical cyclone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone)___ that caused extensive damage and loss of life across the ___E:Antilles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antilles)___ and ___E:Eastern United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_United_States)___ in September 2017. Irma was the first ___E:Category 5 hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category_5_hurricane)___ to strike the ___E:Leeward Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeward_Islands)___ on record, though it was followed by ___E:Hurricane Maria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Maria)___ , which struck the region at Category 5 intensity as well two weeks later.

At the time, Irma was considered the most powerful hurricane on record in the open Atlantic region, outside of the ___E:Caribbean Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea)___ and ___E:Gulf of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico)___ , until it was surpassed by ___E:Hurricane Dorian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dorian)___ two years later.
It was also the third-strongest Atlantic hurricane at landfall ever recorded, just behind the ___E:1935 Labor Day hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1935_Labor_Day_hurricane)___ and Dorian.

The ninth ___E:named storm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_naming)___ , fourth ___E:hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane)___ , second ___E:major hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir%E2%80%93Simpson_scale#Categories)___ , [nb 1] and first ___E:Category 5 hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Category_5_Atlantic_hurricanes)___ of the extremely active ___E:2017 Atlantic hurricane season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Atlantic_hurricane_season)___ , Irma developed from a ___E:tropical wave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave)___ near the ___E:Cape Verde Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Verde)___ on August 30. Favorable conditions allowed Irma to ___E:rapidly intensify U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_intensification)___ into a ___E:Category 3 hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category_3_hurricane)___ on the ___E:Saffir–Simpson wind scale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir%E2%80%93Simpson_wind_scale)___ by late on August 31. The storm's intensity fluctuated between Categories 2 and 3 for the next several days, due to a series of ___E:eyewall replacement cycles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyewall_replacement_cycle)___ .

On September 4, Irma resumed intensifying, becoming a Category 5 hurricane by early on the next day. Early on September 6, Irma peaked with 1-minute sustained winds of 180 mph (290 km/h) and a minimum ___E:pressure U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmospheric_pressure)___ of 914 hPa (27.0 inHg).
Irma was the second-most intense tropical cyclone worldwide in 2017 in terms of barometric pressure, and the strongest worldwide in 2017 in terms of wind speed.

Another eyewall replacement cycle caused Irma to weaken back to a Category 4 hurricane, but the storm re-attained Category 5 status before making landfall in ___E:Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba)___ .

Although Irma briefly weakened to a Category 2 storm while making landfall on Cuba, the system re-intensified to Category 4 status as it crossed the warm waters of the ___E:Straits of Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straits_of_Florida)___ , before making landfall on ___E:Cudjoe Key U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cudjoe_Key,_Florida)___ on September 10. Irma then weakened to Category 3 status, prior to another landfall in Florida on ___E:Marco Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Island,_Florida)___ later that day. The system degraded into a remnant low over ___E:Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama)___ and ultimately dissipated on September 13 over ___E:Missouri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri)___ .

Irma caused widespread and catastrophic damage throughout its long lifetime, particularly in the northeastern ___E:Caribbean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean)___ and the ___E:Florida Keys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Keys)___ .

A ___E:tropical wave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave)___ left the west coast of Africa on August 27, producing a large area of ___E:deep convection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convection_(meteorology))___ .

Over the following days, convection became more concentrated over the northern part of the disturbance, and a surface circulation developed by August 30. The ___E:National Hurricane Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Hurricane_Center)___ (NHC) estimates that the disturbance developed into a tropical depression around 00:00 UTC August 30, about 120 ___E:nautical miles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_miles)___ (138.1 miles; 222.2 kilometers) southwest of the ___E:Cape Verde Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Verde_Islands)___ .

Six hours later, the depression intensified into Tropical Storm Irma, the ninth ___E:named U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_naming)___ storm of the ___E:2017 Atlantic hurricane season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Atlantic_hurricane_season)___ .

Located over warm sea surface temperatures (SSTs), and within an environment of low ___E:wind shear U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_shear#Vertical_component)___ , Irma underwent ___E:rapid intensification U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_intensification)___ .
The formation of an ___E:eye U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_(cyclone))___ around 06:00 UTC on August 31 signified Irma's strengthening into a hurricane, just 30 hours after formation.

Turning to the northwest as the ___E:ridge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridge_(meteorology))___ steering the cyclone weakened, Irma rapidly intensified into a ___E:major hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_hurricane)___ by 00:00 UTC September 1. Within a 48-hour period, the hurricane's intensity had increased by 80 mph (130 km/h).

Fluctuations in intensity occurred over the next few days due to internal processes, as the first ___E:aircraft reconnaissance mission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_hunters)___ into Irma discovered an eye 29 mi (47 km) in diameter and surface winds of 115 mph (185 km/h) on September 3.

As Irma continued approaching the Leeward Islands, the hurricane underwent a second and more robust period of rapid intensification on September 4, becoming a Category 5 hurricane early the following day. The extremely powerful hurricane continued to strengthen, with maximum sustained winds peaking at 180 mph (290 km/h) shortly afterwards.

Irma acquired ___E:annular U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annular_tropical_cyclone)___ characteristics around this time, with the storm exhibiting a large, symmetric ___E:central dense overcast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_dense_overcast)___ (CDO).

At 05:45 UTC on September 6, Irma made landfall along the northern coast of ___E:Barbuda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda)___ at peak intensity, with the storm's central minimum pressure having bottomed out at 914 mbar (27.0 inHg) – this was the lowest minimum pressure in the Atlantic since ___E:Dean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dean)___ in 2007; the storm also made ___E:landfall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall)___ with maximum sustained winds of 180 mph (290 km/h).

Irma continued to maintain its peak intensity until 12:00 UTC on September 6 and made additional successive landfalls on that same day, at 11:15 UTC on ___E:Sint Maarten U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sint_Maarten)___ , and at 16:30 UTC on ___E:Virgin Gorda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Gorda)___ , in the ___E:British Virgin Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Virgin_Islands)___ .
Irma maintained Category 5 strength for several days as it passed north of the ___E:Greater Antilles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Antilles)___ .

After beginning an ___E:eyewall replacement cycle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyewall_replacement_cycle)___ , Irma weakened to a Category 4 hurricane as it passed south of the ___E:Turks and Caicos Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turks_and_Caicos_Islands)___ early on September 8, subsequently ending the 60-hour continuous period of Irma maintaining Category 5 intensity, the second-longest any Atlantic storm had maintained winds above 156 mph (251 km/h) – behind only the ___E:1932 Cuba hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1932_Cuba_hurricane)___ .
The hurricane then began tracking more to the west due to the intensification of a ___E:subtropical ridge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridge_(meteorology))___ to its north.

Once the eyewall replacement cycle was complete, Irma began to re-intensify, and it attained Category 5 intensity for the second time at 18:00 UTC that day east of ___E:Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba)___ .
The very powerful hurricane then made landfall in ___E:Cayo Romano, Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cayo_Romano)___ , at 03:00 UTC on September 9, with winds of 165 mph (266 km/h).
This made Irma only the second Category 5 hurricane to strike Cuba in recorded history, after the ___E:1924 Cuba hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1924_Cuba_hurricane)___ .
As the eye of Irma moved along the northern coast of Cuba, quick weakening ensued due to extended land interaction, with the eye becoming cloud-filled.
Irma bottomed out as a high-end Category 2 storm later on September 9.
After slowing down late that day, the hurricane turned northwestward towards ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida)___ .

This motion resulted from Irma rounding the southwestern edge of the subtropical high to its northeast and a low-pressure system that was located over the continental ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ , to its northwest.

Moving over the warm waters of the Straits of Florida, Irma quickly re-intensified to a Category 4 hurricane at 06:00 UTC on September 10, as deep convection improved and the eye became better defined.

The cyclone made landfall in ___E:Cudjoe Key, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cudjoe_Key,_Florida)___ , at 13:00 UTC on September 10, at Category 4 intensity, with winds of 130 mph (210 km/h).

Increasing wind shear and land interaction caused the satellite appearance of the storm to become ragged later that day, and Irma weakened to Category 3 intensity before making its seventh and final landfall at 19:30 UTC, in ___E:Marco Island, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Island,_Florida)___ , with sustained winds of 115 mph (185 km/h).

Once Irma had moved inland, it began to accelerate to the north-northwest, while rapid weakening began to occur due to the increasing wind shear, land interaction, and dry air, with the storm falling below Category 3 intensity hours after landfall.
Irma finally weakened to a tropical storm on September 11 as it entered southern ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state))___ .

The greatly weakened storm turned more northwestward and degenerated to a remnant low as it crossed into ___E:Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama)___ by 06:00 UTC September 12. The remnant low continued to diminish in strength as it progressed northwestward, dissipating over ___E:Missouri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri)___ the following day.

Hurricane Irma's path was such that its impact was both far-reaching and devastating, with landfalls in ___E:Antigua and Barbuda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua_and_Barbuda)___ , ___E:Saint Martin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Martin_(island))___ , ___E:the Bahamas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bahamas)___ , ___E:Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba)___ , and the United States, all at major hurricane intensity.

Irma is the second-costliest Caribbean hurricane on record, after Maria.

The eyewall of the hurricane moved over ___E:Barbuda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda)___ at its record peak intensity early on September 6; a weather station observed a wind gust of 160 mph (260 km/h).
The same station also recorded a minimum barometric pressure of 916.1 mbar (27.05 inHg).
The exact state of the island remained unclear for hours after Irma's passage, as downed phone lines ceased all communication with nearby islands.
Later that afternoon, Prime Minister ___E:Gaston Browne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaston_Browne)___ surveyed the territory by helicopter, revealing an effectively uninhabitable island.
Irma damaged or destroyed 95% of the structures on Barbuda, including its hospital, schools, and both of its hotels;  it completely flattened some residential blocks while submerging others.
The destruction rendered the island's sole airport and much of its infrastructure inoperative—including water and telecommunication services—which further hampered relief efforts.
Property damage on Barbuda ranged from $150 million to $300 million.
A total of three storm-related deaths were reported on the island.
In addition to the catastrophic impact on Barbuda's human residents, concern turned to the storm's effects on the island's wildlife.

The island's only ___E:endemic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endemic)___ bird, the ___E:near-threatened U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Near-threatened_species)___ ___E:Barbuda warbler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbuda_warbler)___ , numbered less than 2,000 individuals prior to the hurricane.

For some time it was unknown if the warbler survived the hurricane or its aftermath; however within a few months it was confirmed that not only did the species survive, but most of the birds survived the storm.

Barbuda's ___E:Codrington Lagoon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codrington_Lagoon)___ , home to the largest colony of ___E:magnificent frigatebirds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnificent_frigatebird)___ in the Caribbean, with an estimated 2,500 nesting pairs, was also inundated by the storm surge.

Remaining just outside of Irma's strongest windfield, ___E:Antigua U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antigua)___ sustained less severe damage, in the form of leveled roofs and fences, downed power poles and lines, and uprooted trees.
Some street flooding also took place in low-lying areas.

Three people were treated for minor storm-related injuries.  ___E:Forensic disaster analysts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disaster_risk_reduction)___ from the Center for Disaster Management and Risk Reduction Technology (CEDIM), a Germany-based ___E:risk management U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risk_management)___ agency, estimate that economic losses for Antigua and Barbuda will exceed $120 million.

On the morning of September 6, Irma's center crossed the island of ___E:Saint Martin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Martin_(island))___ while the storm was at peak intensity, sweeping away entire structures, submerging roads and cars, and triggering an island-wide blackout.
Irma's extreme winds ripped trees out of the ground and sent vehicles and debris from damaged structures scattered across the territory.

On the French side of ___E:Saint-Martin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collectivity_of_Saint_Martin)___ , entire marinas around ___E:Marigot U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marigot,_Saint_Martin)___ were left in ruins, littered with the stranded remnants of boats that had smashed into each other.
A hotel caught on fire, but dangerous conditions and impassable roads prevented firefighters from putting out the blaze.
Another hotel lost nearly all of its ground floor.
Media images depicted devastated room interiors with furniture hurled around after the winds had shattered their windows.
Irma killed four people on the French side of the island and injured 50 others, one of whom was in critical condition.
As many as 95% of the buildings there were damaged to some degree; 60% of those were totally uninhabitable.
Estimates from CEDIM indicate a minimum of $950 million worth of economic losses.
Total losses exceeded €3.5 billion (US$4.17 billion).

A similar situation unfolded in ___E:Sint Maarten U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sint_Maarten)___ , Saint Martin's Dutch half, as intense winds ripped through buildings and lifted vehicles aloft "as if they were matches".

The hurricane wreaked havoc on ___E:Princess Juliana International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princess_Juliana_International_Airport)___ , with "huge chunks of the building [strewn] across the runway and a jet bridge snapped in half."  It demolished or severely damaged about 70% of Sint Maarten's houses, forcing thousands of residents into public shelters.
There were 4 deaths and 23 injuries,  11 of which were serious, in the Dutch territory.
Irma is considered the worst ___E:natural disaster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_disaster)___ to hit Sint Maarten; the extent of its damage far exceeded that of any previous hurricane.
Total damages were estimated at €2.5 billion (US$2.98 billion).

Irma left widespread destruction and disastrous flooding along its path over the French island of ___E:Saint Barthélemy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Barth%C3%A9lemy)___ , southeast of Saint Martin.

Describing the extent of the destruction, one local compared it to "a bomb that burned all vegetation," while another said that it were as if the hurricane had effectively "erased the island from the map".
Violent seas swept away entire coastal establishments, with one hotel being stripped of all but its foundation.
Streets in the capital of ___E:Gustavia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavia,_Saint_Barth%C3%A9lemy)___ were turned into rushing rivers, which carried away vehicles and pieces of furniture.
The island's fire station was inundated with up to 6.4 ft (2.0 m) of flood waters.
With scores of homes and much of the infrastructure destroyed, the majority of the island's population was left stranded and without water, electricity or phone service.
The associated economic losses could exceed $480 million according to CEDIM's analysts.

This total covered private property such as homes, vehicles and businesses (including lost revenue); the extent of the damage to infrastructural and public facilities remains undetermined.
Nonetheless, this made Irma one of the costliest natural disasters to hit the French Republic in 50 years.
On January 30, 2018, roughly five months after Irma, an analysis was published indicating that an anemometer on the island recorded an unofficial gust to 199 mph (320 km/h) before failing.

The British Overseas Territory of ___E:Anguilla U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anguilla)___ saw the eyewall of the storm pass over it on September 6. Many homes and schools were destroyed, and the island's only hospital was badly damaged.

The devastation was particularly severe in ___E:East End U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_End,_Anguilla)___ , where the winds uprooted scores of trees and power poles and demolished a number of houses.
In ___E:The Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Valley,_Anguilla)___ , the island's capital, the hurricane blew out the windows of government buildings.
Rough seas inflicted heavy damage upon several bays and harbors, and a seaside restaurant was completely eradicated.

The island's air traffic control tower was damaged, exacerbating the already poor communication with the island.
One death was reported on the island.
Estimates of losses on the island total at least $190 million.

One surfer was killed amid rough surf in ___E:Barbados U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados)___ after hitting a reef and breaking his neck. Trees were also destroyed.

Total damage from the three islands was at least $1.1 billion.
The hurricane passed north of ___E:Puerto Rico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico)___ , but still caused significant damage to the United States territory.

At least 30 homes on the island were destroyed, while about 30 other experienced substantial damage.
High winds also toppled a number of trees.

In rural ___E:Loíza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo%C3%ADza,_Puerto_Rico)___ , 79 homes were destroyed.
Throughout Puerto Rico, 781 out of 1,600 telecommunications towers went out of commission, primarily due to power outages.
At least 362,000 customers lost water services.
Debris, mostly fallen trees, blocked at least 72 roads.
Approximately 25% to 30% of banana, coffee, papaya, and plantain crops were damaged by strong winds, with losses to farmers estimated at $30.6 million.
Approximately 1,530 homes experienced at least moderate damage, with 1,448 homes moderately damaged, 32 extensively damaged, and 50 completely destroyed.
Hurricane Irma was attributed to around $1 billion in damage,  and the NHC attributed three fatalities to Irma in Puerto Rico, though four deaths were related to the storm.

Three nearby fishermen were burned by the same lightning strike, but survived.

Two other people died during the hurricane: a woman died while being evacuated from her house in a wheelchair and fell, hitting her head; another person died in a car accident in ___E:Canóvanas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can%C3%B3vanas)___ .

In the immediate aftermath of Hurricane Irma's path through the West Indies and Caribbean, the devastation to roads, harbors and airports significantly impeded the transportation and distribution of relief supplies.
Foreign countries moved to provide much of the initial aid. The British, Dutch, French, and United States governments sent warships and planes with supplies and manpower to the region.

International leaders, including Dutch King ___E:Willem-Alexander U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willem-Alexander)___ and French President ___E:Emmanuel Macron U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Macron)___ , quickly moved to visit affected territories.
Some of the affected countries and territories also offered assistance to each other.
Cuba, which sustained extensive damage from the storm, sent 750 health workers to Antigua and Barbuda, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, The Bahamas, Dominica, and Haiti.
Government officials and members of the public in Puerto Rico delivered assistance and evacuated people stranded on other islands.

The ___E:U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Citizenship_and_Immigration_Services)___ granted special 30-day humanitarian visas for British Virgin Islanders to stay in Puerto Rico.  Hundreds of people stranded on Saint Martin were flown to the Dominican Republic on humanitarian grounds.
In response to Hurricane Jose's approach, the Government of Antigua and Barbuda issued a mandatory evacuation on September 9 for any remaining residents on Barbuda.
A Miami cargo plane landed on Antigua later that day, carrying over 60 tons (120,000 lbs) of relief supplies for the displaced storm victims—including bottled water, canned food and power generators.

___E:RFA Mounts Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RFA_Mounts_Bay_(L3008))___ stationed itself near Anguilla and provided support and relief work to the island with its helicopters and 40 marines and army engineers.

The ship delivered 6 tonnes of emergency aid to Anguilla and army engineers repaired a fuel leak at Anguilla's main petrol dump, restored power to the island's hospital and provided shelters for those left homeless by the hurricane.

The ship arrived in the British Virgin Islands on September 8, 2017, to provide emergency relief to the islands, including providing shelters, food and water.  ___E:HMS Ocean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ocean_(L12))___ was diverted from the ___E:Mediterranean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea)___ to provide relief from ___E:Gibraltar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar)___ to the affected British Overseas Territories of Anguilla, British Virgin Islands and Turks and Caicos on September 7,  and aid was also supplied by the ___E:Department for International Development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_for_International_Development)___ from their disaster response center at ___E:Kemble Airfield U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kemble_Airfield)___ .

As part of a £32 million operation named Operation Ruman, nearly 500 UK military personnel with emergency relief were dispatched from ___E:RAF Brize Norton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAF_Brize_Norton)___ .

This included the first deployment of ___E:No. 38 Expeditionary Air Wing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No._38_Expeditionary_Air_Wing)___ with three RAF aircraft: two Airbus A400M Atlas and one C-130J Hercules to support relief efforts.

The British government also drafted two members of the UK police cadre into the region on September 10, and 53 police officers were drafted from RAF Brize Norton to the affected British Overseas Territories on September 15 to help maintain order.
UK politicians, including the chairs of the foreign affairs and development select committees, criticized both the government's preparations for the storm and its response as inadequate.

By September 12, the Department for International Development had delivered more than 40 tonnes of aid into the region, including into Turks and Caicos, and 1,000 UK military troops were deployed in the region as part of relief efforts.

The ___E:Prime Minister of the United Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Kingdom)___ , ___E:Theresa May U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theresa_May)___ , pledged an additional £25 million worth of funding as part of relief efforts in the region on September 13, 2017, and the ___E:Secretary of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_State_for_Foreign_and_Commonwealth_Affairs)___ , ___E:Boris Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Johnson)___ , said that a further 250 UK military personnel would be deployed into the area within the next few days.  Anguilla's Chief Minister, ___E:Victor Banks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Banks)___ , praised the British government's response to the storm and said that Boris Johnson's visit to the island "sends a very positive signal to Anguillans that the British are serious about their response to this very severe hurricane", but went on to say that the current financial commitment from the UK was not substantial enough.
By September 15, the United Kingdom had over 70 military personnel and 4 police officers in Anguilla and had delivered 15 tonnes of aid to the island.

In the British Virgin Islands, Royal Marines had cleared the airfield so that it was operational for the delivery of aid into the islands, with more than 200 British military personnel and 54 UK police officers on the ground and 8 tonnes of aid delivered to the islands.  120 British military personnel were on the ground in Turks and Caicos, and over 150 shelter kits and 720 liters of water were delivered to the islands on September 15.

Amendments to international aid rules by the ___E:Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organisation_for_Economic_Co-operation_and_Development)___ (or OECD) allowed for the UK government to provide access to £13 billion worth of aid to the affected British Overseas Territories, through the UK's ___E:Official Development Assistance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Development_Assistance)___ (ODA) by November 2017.

The worst devastation occurred on ___E:Ragged Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ragged_Island,_Bahamas)___ , over which Irma's eye had directly passed.
